rationale: Formal check for the recovery-vbal Candidate: the exploration reproduced the mechanism in a clean copy, so this product fixes the requirement and the oracle. The obligation is that a slow-quorum reply reporting the instance COMMITTED must be adopted by the recovering replica; the harness reaches the resolution with a prepared COMMITTED peer record and a default local record and emits canonical events, and the monitor decides whether the resolution adopted it. The plan names the two bindings that carry the requirement (the recovery entry and the resolution loop) so the check can be reviewed against the encoded predicate rather than only against its output.

candidate.rationale: The obligation and bindings are supplied together with the check so the claim exists before the plan references it; the requirement is a recovery duty, not the earlier fast-path question.

question.question: When recovery runs for instance (Replica, Instance) and a slow-quorum PrepareReply reports that instance COMMITTED with a command vector, does the recovering replica adopt that committed vector, or does it continue from its own record and restart phase 1 with a different command (NOOP when its record has no commands)?
question.importance: If the committed vector is not adopted, the replicas that already committed and possibly executed the instance keep it while the recovering replica re-proposes another command, so the instance has two competing values: an installed commit that ignores later Commits versus a re-proposal that can be accepted by replicas that do not hold the commit. That is an agreement and state-convergence concern for a crash-recovered replica.
contexts: recovering replica holding a default NONE record
peer holding COMMITTED with a command
event_paths: startRecoveryForInstance seeds the local record and reports the new ballot as its own VBallot
the peer's PrepareReply reports Status COMMITTED at an older vbal
handlePrepareReply resolves and either adopts the committed vector or restarts phase 1

supporting_behavior_ids.B11-prepare-resolution: the highest-vbal selection and sub-case dispatch that decides adoption
supporting_behavior_ids.B6-commit-install: shows what a committed replica reports
supporting_behavior_ids.B10-prepare-acceptor: shows the Ballot/VBallot a remote replica reports after joining the new ballot

counterevidence: scoped to the source: the resolution rule compares element.VBallot against a running lb.ballot seeded from the record's old vbal while the self PrepareReply reports the new ballot, so the comparison order decides adoption (S14-recovery-start-prepare, S15-handlePrepareReply)

scoped to the launched configuration: makeBallot can also return a ballot below a remote vbal that was raised by an earlier recovery, which would change which replies pass the test (S5-broadcasters, S24-runReplica-epaxos)
unknowns: whether a full legal history reaches the same state
whether the recovering replica's accept phase can still complete when the committed replica refuses to store the new attributes (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply)
question.trigger_rationale: The exploration run in a clean copy showed the recovering replica reporting the new ballot as its own VBallot, skipping the peer's COMMITTED reply at vbal 0 and restarting phase 1 with NOOP; this check fixes that observation as a requirement with an explicit oracle.

obligation.description: When recovery runs for instance (Replica, Instance) and a slow-quorum PrepareReply reports that instance COMMITTED with a command vector, the recovering replica must adopt that committed vector (Status COMMITTED carrying the committed commands) rather than continuing from its own record and restarting phase 1 with a different command.

scope.description: Recovery decision for a single instance on the captured snapshot: N=3 with Thrifty and IsLeader false, the recovering replica holding only a default NONE record, one peer holding a COMMITTED record with a real command, and no third replica reply required.
assumptions: the recovering replica's own record carries no commands
a slow quorum (its own entry plus one reply) is sufficient to resolve
messages are delivered through the real wire format
excluded: producing the committed record through a real proposal, accept round and commit broadcast
execution of the instance and client-visible replies
configurations with N>3 or a live leader flag

grounding.derivation: Recovery exists to carry the value that could have been committed across a change of leader. In this snapshot the recovering replica seeds its bookkeeping from its own record, makes a new ballot and reports that new ballot as its own VBallot, while handlePrepareReply keeps the attributes of a reply only when element.VBallot >= the running lb.ballot. The responsibility asserted here is that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED must be adopted, because a committed record is the authoritative value for that instance and is the only input that can keep the recovering replica consistent with replicas that already installed the commit.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the captured snapshot with N=3 and Thrifty, IsLeader false, the recovering replica holding a default NONE record for the instance and one slow-quorum peer holding a COMMITTED record with a command; the recovery is entered directly through startRecoveryForInstance.
unresolved: whether a full legal history (real proposal, accept round, commit broadcast, execution timeout) reaches the same state
whether the launched configuration permits a replica to hold a default record for an instance that another replica has committed
alternatives: an alternative reading is that the recovering replica is only required to adopt the value with the highest vbal and that the local record's new ballot legitimately outranks an older committed vbal, which the review should test against the cited resolution code

associations.rationale: The entry decides which vbal the recovering replica reports and therefore which remote replies the resolution may adopt.

bindings.description: Recovery entry that seeds the leader bookkeeping from the local record, makes the new ballot and reports the record's vbal in its own PrepareReply.

associations.rationale: The loop applies element.VBallot >= lb.ballot and assigns lb.cmds/lb.status from the passing element, so a COMMITTED reply is only adopted when it passes that test; otherwise the resolution falls to the phase-1 restart.

bindings.description: Resolution of PrepareReply values: highest-vbal selection, status-based sub-case choice and the restart of phase 1.
